classification.difficultyReason: Explore rectangle dimensions with a fixed perimeter and identify the maximum area without restricting side lengths to whole numbers.

content.prompt: Chase and Lana have 108 m of fencing with which to enclose an area of the schoolyard for a rectangular garden. Explore the possible areas of their garden, and state which alternative has the largest area.

answer.short:
The largest area is $729\text{ m}^2$, for a square measuring $27\text{ m}\times27\text{ m}$.

With a fixed perimeter, the area increases as the adjacent side lengths become closer to equal.
answer.worked:
The two lengths and two widths total $108$ m, so one length and one width total $108\div2=54$ m. Some possible dimensions and areas are:
$$\begin{align*}A_{1\text{ m}\times53\text{ m}}&=1\times53=53\text{ m}^2\\A_{10\text{ m}\times44\text{ m}}&=10\times44=440\text{ m}^2\\A_{20\text{ m}\times34\text{ m}}&=20\times34=680\text{ m}^2\\A_{25\text{ m}\times29\text{ m}}&=25\times29=725\text{ m}^2\\A_{26\text{ m}\times28\text{ m}}&=26\times28=728\text{ m}^2\\A_{26.5\text{ m}\times27.5\text{ m}}&=26.5\times27.5=728.75\text{ m}^2\\A_{27\text{ m}\times27\text{ m}}&=27\times27=729\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
For a fixed sum of adjacent side lengths, bringing the lengths closer together increases their product. This also applies to fractional side lengths. The largest area therefore occurs when the lengths are equal: a $27$ m by $27$ m square, with area $729\text{ m}^2$.
